Ch2: 함정 구간 전수 보존 — 파피루스 바구니·역청·아스팔트 방수, 누나의 거리 유지 감시, 바로 딸의 목욕·시녀·바구니 발견, 모세(Pulled-Out)·십보라(Bird)·게르솜(Sojourner) 이름 뜻, 르우엘, 일곱 딸·구유·양, 미디안 우물, 언약 기억(아브라함·이삭·야곱)
paragraphs: A guy from the tribe of Levi married a Levite woman. She got pregnant and had a baby boy. She could tell there was something special about him, so she hid him. She kept him hidden for three months. When she couldn't hide him anymore, she made a little basket-boat out of papyrus, sealed it up with tar and pitch to make it waterproof, and put the baby inside. Then she set it floating in the reeds at the edge of the Nile.

The baby's big sister stayed at a distance, watching to see what would happen. Then Pharaoh's daughter came down to the Nile to take a bath, with her servants strolling along the bank. She spotted the basket-boat floating in the reeds and sent one of her maids to grab it. She opened it — and there was the baby, crying! Her heart melted. She said, "This must be one of the Hebrew babies."
Then his sister stepped up: "Want me to go find a Hebrew woman to nurse the baby for you?"
Pharaoh's daughter said, "Yes, go!" So the girl ran and got the baby's own mother.
Pharaoh's daughter told her, "Take this baby and nurse him for me — I'll pay you." The woman took the child and nursed him.
Once the boy was weaned, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, who adopted him as her own son. She named him Moses — "Pulled-Out" — saying, "I pulled him out of the water."

Years went by and Moses grew up. One day he went out to see his fellow Israelites and watched them doing brutal slave labor. Then he saw an Egyptian beating up a Hebrew — one of his own people! He looked around; nobody was watching. So he killed the Egyptian and buried him in the sand.
The next day he went back out and saw two Hebrew men fighting. He said to the one who started it, "Why are you hitting your neighbor?"
The guy snapped back, "Who do you think you are, bossing us around? You gonna kill me like you killed that Egyptian?" Moses panicked — "Uh oh. People know about this."
When Pharaoh heard about it, he tried to have Moses killed. But Moses ran for it and escaped to Midian. He sat down by a well.

The priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came to draw water, filling up the troughs to water their father's sheep. Some shepherds showed up and chased the girls off — but Moses jumped in to rescue them and helped them water their sheep.
When they got home to their dad Reuel, he said, "Wow, you're back early. How come?"
"Some Egyptian guy," they said, "rescued us from those shepherds. He even drew water for us and watered the sheep!"
He said, "Well, where is he? Why'd you leave him out there? Invite him in to eat with us!"

Moses decided to stay with the man, who gave him his daughter Zipporah — "Bird" — as his wife. She had a son, and Moses named him Gershom — "Sojourner" — saying, "I'm a stranger living in a foreign land."
A lot of years passed, and the king of Egypt died. But the Israelites were still groaning under slavery, crying out for help. Their cries rose all the way up to God.
God heard their groaning. God remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God saw what was happening to Israel. God understood.
title: Moses Is Born
